Subject: Calibrating interview focus & leveling for Sr Inference Eng (Westwater)

Hi team,

I pulled together a quick leveling matrix and a proposed mapping of interviewers to focus areas for the Westwater Sr. Inference Eng role — attaching v2 of the matrix and a draft scorecard. Key asks:

- Can we confirm who will act as the bar-raiser?
- Agree on the scope we expect at L5 vs L6 for this role (system architecture breadth, infra ownership, model ops proficiency).
- Call out 3 redline topics we want every interviewer to probe (kv/cache design, productionization of custom kernels, post-deployment troubleshooting).

I mapped:
- Systems & infra: Dev
- Model & serving correctness: Hannah
- Ownership & cross-team impact: Lauren

Pls review the attached leveling_matrix_v2.xlsx and sr-inference-scorecard.docx and reply with any edits. I also included the candidate's resume in the drive link for reference.

Thanks,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-01T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calibrating interview focus & leveling for Sr Inference Eng (Westwater)

Thanks Marissa — this is a helpful start. A few quick thoughts:

- Bar-raiser: I agree we should pick someone not on the interview loop day-of. Suggest Markus Klein as bar-raiser; he has recent infra + distributed systems hiring context.
- Leveling expectations: For L6 I want explicit deliverables around:
  * leading a cross-functional rollout (owner of rollout plan + incident runbook)
  * measurable latency/throughput improvements via kernel/serving changes
  * mentorship of other engineers on inference best practices

- Interview focus areas to standardize across panel (short checklist to ensure parity):
  1) Problem decomposition + trade-offs (30%)
  2) End-to-end production ownership (40%)
  3) Behavioral leadership & stakeholder communication (30%)

Optional: we should add a short prompt for interviewers to ask the candidate to sketch a KV cache mitigation for a 99.99% tail latency incident — that'll separate good system thinkers.

I can take ownership of the model-serving correctness panel. Will update the scorecard with the checklist.

—Hannah
Hiring Manager, Inference Services
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calibrating interview focus & leveling for Sr Inference Eng (Westwater)

+1 to Markus as bar-raiser. A couple of technical clarifications from my side:

- For L6 we should expect comfort with at least one custom kernel/quantization flow and the ability to reason about memory layout trade-offs. Not just conceptual — we should ask them to walk through a concrete optimization they shipped.
- Interviewers should have a kernel / ops case (45min):
  * 15m: candidate explains previous optimization end-to-end
  * 20m: whiteboard a rollout + rollback strategy with metrics and SLO guardrails
  * 10m: follow-ups on edge cases (memory fragmentation, NUMA effects)

I attached a brief template (sr-inference-scorecard.docx) that includes a technical rubric. Also, I propose the bar-raiser receives a compiled packet with notes from all interviewers before final call — it'll help calibration.

Dev
Staff Serving Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-06-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Calibrating interview focus & leveling for Sr Inference Eng (Westwater)

Nice. Two additions:

1) Behavioral anchors: we should give interviewers 3 behavior snippets to rate against (Ownership, Influence, Prioritization). I'll paste those into the doc.
2) Leveling nuance: call out where we draw the line on "breadth" vs "depth". L5 = deep contributor on 1–2 inference subsystems; L6 = leads design across multiple stacks and drives cross-team delivery.

Also: small practical note — can we standardize the rejection wording for near-miss L5 vs L6 cases so recruiting can provide useful feedback? I've got a short paragraph for that too.

Link to draft playbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcLevelingPlaybook/edit

—Lauren
